neighbours.label: ' to' or an adverb after a word of tendency or willingness (likely to, chose to, afraid to, rarely, couldn't help but), as opposed to the same sentences stating plain facts
fire: She is one of the loudest critics and is likely to stay that way.
Family doctors rarely test for this infection.
He couldn't help but smile at the news.
I decided to take a picture of the old bridge.
Never be scared to ask for directions.
The board is unlikely to approve the plan.
Most buyers tend to choose the cheaper model.
He refused to sign the letter.
quiet: She is one of the loudest critics in the town.
Family doctors in this town are busy.
He smiled at the news on the radio.
I took a picture of the old bridge.
Never put metal in the microwave.
The board met in the plan room.
Most buyers come from the nearby town.
He signed the letter in blue ink.

short: tendency or willingness before a verb
notes: Card flags this pole as broad (1.5%), with ' student' and ' I' also near the top, so this covers a part.
